entities.name: Andreas Räss
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Andreas Räss (born April 6, 1794, Sigolsheim – died November 17, 1887, Strasbourg) served as the influential Catholic Bishop of Strasbourg for over four decades, from 1842 until his death. A pivotal figure in the religious landscape of Alsace during the 19th century, Räss navigated the complex interplay of French and German cultural influences and the burgeoning struggle between Gallican and Ultramontane Catholicism. His episcopacy was marked by a steadfast commitment to Roman orthodoxy and a deep engagement with theological scholarship, profoundly shaping the ecclesiastical identity of the region.

Educated at the seminary in Mainz and the universities of Heidelberg and Freiburg im Breisgau, Räss began his career as a professor of theology and later served as a cathedral canon in Strasbourg. His intellectual prowess was evident in his extensive literary output, notably his collaboration with Johannes Baptist von Weiss on the multi-volume 'Leben der Heiligen und Seligen' (Lives of Saints and Blessed), a monumental work of hagiography that propagated Catholic piety across German-speaking lands. As Bishop, Räss championed the revitalization of Catholic education, established numerous religious orders within his diocese, and staunchly defended papal authority against liberal theological currents, particularly during the lead-up to the First Vatican Council.

Räss's long tenure as Bishop solidified Ultramontane Catholicism in Alsace, ensuring that the diocese remained firmly aligned with Rome amidst the broader European religious shifts. His efforts in seminary reform and the promotion of a devout, disciplined clergy left a lasting imprint on the local church, fostering a generation of priests committed to traditional doctrine. His resistance to governmental interference in church affairs, a characteristic stance of Ultramontane bishops, also reinforced the autonomy of the Catholic hierarchy in the region, influencing future church-state relations.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Andreas Räss was a highly significant regional figure, who through his 45-year episcopacy, profoundly shaped the direction of the Catholic Church in Alsace by championing Ultramontanism and reforming clerical education, ensuring its Roman alignment through periods of intense political and theological change.
